subject: Insurance
title: The Costa Concordia Tragedy
description: A quick, practical guide to The Costa Concordia Tragedy.

hook.text: In 2012, the Costa Concordia capsized off Italy, killing 32 people. The total insurance claim reached $2 billion.

buildup.text: The captain steered dangerously close to shore to 'salute' the island.

discovery.text: The wreck removal alone cost $1.5 billion—the most expensive salvage in maritime history.

twist.text: The captain was convicted of manslaughter. But the ship was insured.

climax.text: Costa Concordia proved that even modern cruise ships with GPS can sink from human error.

punchline.text: $2 billion claim from a show-off captain. Human error sinks the biggest ships.

quiz.question: What caused the Costa Concordia disaster?
options: The captain steered dangerously close to shore
